'''Gloria Lubkin''' ({{Nee}} '''Becker'''; May 16, 1933 – January 26, 2020) was an American science journalist and editor for the magazine ''[[Physics Today]]'', of which she was the [[editor-in-chief]] from 1985 to 1994.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Wayne|first=Tiffany K.|title=American Women of Science since 1900|url=https://archive.org/details/americanwomensci00phdt|url-access=limited|publisher=ABC-CLIO|year=2011|isbn=978-1-59884-158-9|pages=[https://archive.org/details/americanwomensci00phdt/page/n664 638]-639}}</ref> She also cofounded the Theoretical Physics Institute at the [[University of Minnesota]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://pswscience.org/meeting/adventures-of-a-physics-reporter/|title=Adventures of a Physics Reporter - Gloria Lubkin|website=PSW Science|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-22}}</ref> and was a fellow of both the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

== Early life and education ==
Lubkin was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania on May 16, 1933, to a Jewish family. At age 16, she enrolled at [[Temple University]], where she graduated with a BS in Physics in 1953. In 1957, she earned an MA in nuclear physics from [[Boston University]],<ref name=":1" /> under the supervision of [[Fay Ajzenberg-Selove]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|date=2020-02-11|title=Gloria Lubkin (1933–2020)|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.6.4.20200211a/abs/|journal=Physics Today|volume=2020|issue=4|article-number=0211a|language=EN|doi=10.1063/PT.6.4.20200211a|bibcode=2020PhT..2020d.211. |s2cid=243188138 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

She married Yale Jay Lubkin, son of computer scientist [[Samuel Lubkin]], in 1953, and they had two children before divorcing in 1968.

== Career ==
After earning her master's, Lubkin worked as a mathematician at [[Fairchild Industries|Fairchild Stratos]]. As a nuclear physicist for TRG Inc, she designed shielding for nuclear reactors and [[nuclear-powered aircraft]]. She also worked at [[LIU Post|C.W. Post]] as an assistant professor, and was acting physics chair at [[Sarah Lawrence College]] from 1961 to 1962.<ref name=":0" />

In 1963, Lubkin [[Cold calling|cold-called]] ''Physics Today'', looking for a position as a science journalist. She was soon fired, however, when it was discovered she was pregnant. She was rehired in 1965, six weeks after the birth of her daughter, and stayed at ''Physics Today'' for 45 years. Over the course of her career, she served as associate editor (1963–70), senior editor (1970–84), editor-in-chief (1985–94),<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|date=2008-01-04|title=Thoughts on Becoming Editor|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.2814622|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=38|issue=6|page=128|doi=10.1063/1.2814622|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> editorial director (1995–2000), editor-at-large (2001–03), and editor emerita (2004–09). She prepared special issues of the magazine dedicated to Physics in [[Japan]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|date=2008-01-11|title=Special Issue: Physics in Japan|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.2820306|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=40|issue=12|page=25|doi=10.1063/1.2820306|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Richard Feynman]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|date=2008-01-08|title=Special Issue: Richard Feynman|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.881188|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=42|issue=2|pages=22–23|doi=10.1063/1.881188|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[Andrei Sakharov]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|date=2008-01-11|title=Special Issue: Andrei Sakharov|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.2810651|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=43|issue=8|page=25|doi=10.1063/1.2810651|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> as well as for its 50th anniversary.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|date=2008-01-11|title=A Personal Look Back at Physics Today|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.882227|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=51|issue=5|pages=24–29|doi=10.1063/1.882227|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Her final story for the magazine<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|date=2013-05-31|title=Fay Ajzenberg-Selove|journal=Physics Today|volume=66|issue=6|page=62|doi=10.1063/PT.3.2018|bibcode=2013PhT....66f..62L|issn=0031-9228|doi-access=free}}</ref> was an [[obituary]] for the nuclear physicist [[Fay Ajzenberg-Selove]], one of the few women physicists to have received the [[National Medal of Science]].

Lubkin was one of the first American science journalists to travel to the [[Soviet Union]] (in 1968)<ref>{{Citation|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|title=A Visit to the Physics Institute of the USSR Academy of Sciences|journal=Physics Today|date=1968-11-01|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.3034589|volume=21|issue=11|pages=57–59|type=letter|language=en|doi=10.1063/1.3034589|bibcode=1968PhT....21k..57L|access-date=2020-02-21|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and to the [[China|People's Republic of China]] (in 1979).<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lubkin|first=Gloria B.|date=1980-03-01|title=Physics Today in China|url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.2913995|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=33|issue=3|pages=32–39|doi=10.1063/1.2913995|bibcode=1980PhT....33c..32L|issn=0031-9228|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In China she toured laboratories in Shanghai and Beijing, and attended a televised meeting of physicists in the [[Great Hall of the People]].<ref name=":1" />

At the American Physical Society, Lubkin was very active in the Forum on the History of Physics, serving in a variety of roles. In 1970 she cofounded the Committee on the Status of Women in Physics at APS. She became a [[Nieman Fellowship|Nieman Fellow]] of Harvard University in 1974,<ref name=":1" /> and later served on the Nieman advisory committee and the selection committee for [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]]'s [[Knight Science Journalism]] Fellowships.<ref name=":0" /> She was named a Fellow of the AAAS in 1986.

As a recognition of her role<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cse.umn.edu/ftpi/about-us|title=About Us {{!}} William I. Fine Theoretical Physics Institute {{!}} College of Science and Engineering|website=cse.umn.edu|access-date=2020-02-28}}</ref> in helping to found the [[William I. Fine Theoretical Physics Institute]] at the University of Minnesota, the Gloria Becker Lubkin Professorship of Theoretical Physics was established there in 1990.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/809-katharine-gebbie-and-gloria-lubkin-join-the-department-of-physics.html|title=Katharine Gebbie and Gloria Lubkin Join the Department of Physics - UMD Physics|website=umdphysics.umd.edu|access-date=2020-02-22}}</ref> In 2013, she was awarded the title of visiting senior research scholar at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] Department of Physics.<ref name=":2" />
